title: Grateful Dead Live at Grand Prix Racecourse on 1973-07-28
lineage: Soundboard Master Reel>DAT>CD>SHN , with FM, AUD, and other-source SBD patches.

ai_review.summary: Soundboard recording of the legendary Watkins Glen show – solid audio that’s a bit thin in spots but captures an electrifying performance highlighted by Mountain Jam and a soaring China‑Cat > I Know You Rider.
ai_review.review: The SBD capture is generally clear with occasional analog hiss and a thin low end, yet it conveys the historic vibe of the 600‑thousand‑person gathering. Musically the show shines – the Allman‑brothers‑enhanced Mountain Jam, an inspired China‑Cat > I Know You Rider, and strong renditions of Eyes of the World, Stella Blue and others make it a fan favorite, even if a few listeners find the China jam uneven.

ai_rating.rationale: The overwhelming majority of reviews (≈70 %) award 4‑5 stars and praise the performance; recording quality is described as good/clear with only occasional complaints, yielding a strong combined score.

recording_quality.technical_notes: Generally crisp and clear soundboard mix; some reviewers note analog "crunch", thin high‑end, occasional static and a few AUD clicks. Early in the show drums are recessed before the board settles, but overall the tape is listenable.

standout_songs: China Cat > I Know You Rider
poor_songs: China Cat > I Know You Rider (criticized by a minority as sloppy)
show_quality.setlist_flow: The show is remembered as a massive, jam‑heavy event that built momentum from the early soundcheck through a long first set, then exploded with the Allmans and The Band on the encore. Highlights flow naturally – Mountain Jam opens the second half, followed by tight group improvisations and classic Dead numbers.

band_member_comments.Jerry: Praised for soaring guitar tone and soulful playing; a few note occasional sloppiness in the China jam.
band_member_comments.Phil: His bass work is highlighted as strong and ‘lots of Phil’, even cited for drinking 24 Heinekens during the set.
band_member_comments.Keys: Keyboard work (Keith) noted positively, especially on tracks like Eyes of the World; some reviews simply say “lots of Keith/Phil”.
band_member_comments.Drums: Early mix issues left drums thin or absent for a few minutes; later the percussion settles and supports the jams.
